description: Open a session with ONE call instead of four. Returns this workspace's guide (its operating manual - follow it), the catchup delta since your agent last looked, the project's memory as an INDEX (titles, one-line hooks and ids - NOT bodies; recall an id for the full text), and your inbox count with a short preview. Pass `project` to scope the index (use resolve_project to find it from a working directory); `space` to pick a workspace. Compact by design - `memory_total` greater than the index length, `catchup_more`, or `truncated=true` mean there is more to page with recall/catchup. Call it FIRST, before doing anything else in a workspace; it consumes the catchup delta like catchup does (set `peek: true` to leave the cursor).

peek.description:
peek reads the catchup delta without advancing the cursor. Default false:
 brief is the session opener, so it consumes the delta like catchup does.

project.description:
project optionally scopes the memory index to one project (a project-kind
 tag name, or the value from resolve_project); empty briefs the whole
 workspace.

space.description:
space optionally selects which of your spaces to brief (an id or name from
 list_spaces). Omit it when you belong to a single space.

name: brief

catchup.description:
catchup lists, compactly, what changed since this instance last looked
 (publishes, versions, feedback, promotions) - excluding your own instance's
 writes. catchup_more counts entries beyond this list; first_look is true for
 a brand-new instance with no delta window yet.

guide.description: guide is the workspace operating manual - the house rules for working here.

inboxCount.description:
inbox_count is how many items await you across your workspaces; headlines is
 a short preview of the most recent.

memoryIndex.description:
memory_index is the project's memory as titles + one-line hooks + ids, NOT
 bodies - enough to know what exists and whether it matters, then fetch by id.

hook.description:
hook is a one-line snippet - enough to know whether the memory matters,
 NOT the body. Fetch the full memory by id (recall) when it does.

title.description: title is what the memory is about.

memoryTotal.description:
memory_total is how many memories are in scope; the index may be capped to
 keep the brief compact, so total greater than len(memory_index) means there
 is more - recall to page it.

project.description: project is the scope the index reflects (empty = the whole workspace).

startHere.description:
start_here is set ONLY when this workspace holds no memories at all, and it
 carries what to do about that (#153). An empty workspace is the one state
 where every other field is blank and the tools all look broken: recall
 returns nothing, so the assistant reasonably concludes Kythene has nothing
 to offer and stops calling it - the workspace then stays empty forever.
 This is the instruction that breaks that loop, and it is delivered HERE
 because brief is the one call every client is told to make first, whether
 it loaded a skill, a plugin or nothing at all. It disappears by itself the
 moment the workspace has content, so it can never become stale advice.

 Do not confuse it with first_look, which is about this INSTANCE's cursor: a
 brand-new instance connecting to a mature workspace sets first_look and
 must NOT be given onboarding.

truncated.description:
truncated is true when any list here was capped to keep the brief small, so
 a reader knows it has not seen everything (rather than mistaking the cap for
 the whole - the manufactured-absence trap).

title: Open a session
